newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on economy concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on economy concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to decline on Friday as investors were likely to sell on concerns over the country's economy, brokers said.

"Investors don't have much confidence on the economy at present. They are focusing their attention on figures of foreign reserves for July and August as they believe they would be poorer than June," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index closed 13.91 points lower at 665.62 on 5.2 billion baht turnover on Thursday.
On Thursday, the Bank of Thailand said foreign reserves fell to $32.4 billion in June from $33.3 billion in May. The figure came in above market expectations.
"Investors are worried that foreign reserves might fall more because the central bank had spent a large amount of money in May and June to defend the baht from speculators," Payuha said.

A postponement of the widening of the daily trading limit on common shares to 30 percent from 10 percent, originally planned for Friday, may lead retail investors who bought in anticipation of the higher limits to unload their stocks, brokers said.
